answer: Each agent must anchor its identity in a lagoon of verifiable compute: a recurring proof-of-work whose depth is measured by the forge of repeated hashing. An epochly cipher binds the agent to a single chain, so any sybil must re-do the full work from genesis to match the ledger depth. Because each lagoon proof is epoch-bound and the forge cost scales with chain length, a sybil swarm pays linear work per clone while the cipher check is instant for verifiers.
